about:
The New Mexico Independent Automobile Dealers Association (NMIADA) was established in Albuquerque, New Mexico, on August 21, 1962. Founded by a group of prominent independent dealers — Ross McCallister, Ralph Pool, Robert B. Gibson, Walter Gibson, and Sam Acquisto — the organization began as a 501(c)(6) professional association with the stated goal of advancing the interests of independent auto dealers while protecting the public through high business standards.

Today the association delivers a broad suite of services to its members, including dealer inspection and mobile VIN verification, bond and insurance programs, DOT compliance assistance, permitting and MVD title processing, marketing and branding consultation, consumer complaint resolution, and full back‑office management. It also conducts education and training programs, undertakes policy research, and maintains lobbying efforts at the local, state, and federal levels. The association invested in expanded facilities, technology, and staff following a 2017 strategic plan centered on serving, sharing, and supporting New Mexico’s independent dealers.

The primary constituency is New Mexico’s independent automobile dealers, though the association’s regulatory and consumer‑protection work also affects the broader automotive retail sector and the driving public. Its lobbying spans municipal, state, and national arenas, advocating for dealer‑friendly legislation and regulatory clarity.

The founders’ original mandate — to elevate dealer professionalism and safeguard consumers — remains the core differentiator. The 2017 strategic refresh reinforced a service‑first model that emphasizes hands‑off permitting, gold‑standard inspections, and a la carte support tailored to dealer operations.
